record.paper_title: Observations and Open Questions in Beam-Beam Interactions
record.original_question: For possible future LHC crab-cavity operation, how sensitive are the beams to cavity phase noise and to synchro-betatron resonances driven by dispersion in the crab cavities, and are there additional beam-dynamics limitations that detailed studies should uncover before implementation?

evidence.quote: Some issues require detailed studies such as the sensitivity of the beam to phase noise in the cavities, synchro-betatron resonances driven by dispersion in these cavities and perhaps others.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a high-energy circular hadron collider (such as the LHC) equipped with transverse deflecting "crab" RF cavities used to compensate the geometric luminosity loss arising from a finite crossing angle at the interaction points. A bunch is described by its 6-D phase-space coordinates, and the crab cavities impart a transverse momentum kick whose magnitude depends on the longitudinal position of each particle (and on the cavity phase relative to the synchronous particle). Two specific effects are of interest:

1. Cavity phase noise. Suppose the crab-cavity RF phase fluctuates stochastically with a power spectral density S(f). Derive quantitative expressions and tolerance limits relating S(f) (and amplitude noise) to the resulting transverse emittance growth rate of the stored beam, taking into account the betatron tune spread and the synchrotron sidebands. Determine the maximum allowable noise level (over the relevant frequency band) such that the emittance growth and luminosity lifetime remain compatible with collider operation.

2. Synchro-betatron resonances driven by dispersion in the crab cavities. With nonzero dispersion D and dispersion derivative D' at the location of the crab cavity, classify and quantify the synchro-betatron resonance conditions m·Q_x + n·Q_y + p·Q_s = integer that are excited (including those introduced by the crab kick itself and higher-order multipole content of the cavity field), compute their driving terms and stop-band widths, and assess their impact on dynamic aperture and beam lifetime for off-momentum particles.

Finally, identify and analyze any additional beam-dynamics limitations (e.g., impedance-coupling with crab-cavity noise, long-range and head-on beam-beam interplay, nonlinear multipole content) that constrain the operability of crab cavities in such a collider, and establish the corresponding tolerance budget.
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made since the question was posed. Theory, simulations, and beam-based measurements relating crab-cavity RF noise to transverse emittance growth have been published (e.g., Phys. Rev. Accel. Beams 27, 051001 (2024) on noise-driven emittance growth and 27, 071001 (2024) on impedance effects), and synchro-betatron resonances driven by crab cavities and large Piwinski angle have been analyzed (Phys. Rev. Accel. Beams 24, 041002 (2021); HL-LHC studies). Tolerances and cures have been derived and partially validated experimentally, but ongoing HL-LHC commissioning continues to refine the full set of beam-dynamics limitations, so the broader question is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Transverse emittance growth due to rf noise in crab cavities
status_evidence.snippet: Theory, measurements, cure, and high luminosity LHC estimates of emittance growth from crab-cavity rf noise.
status_evidence.claim: Quantitative theory and measurements relating crab-cavity phase/amplitude noise to emittance growth have been established.

status_evidence.title: Synchrobetatron resonance of crab crossing scheme with large crossing angle and finite bunch length
status_evidence.snippet: Higher-order synchrobetatron resonances excited in crab crossing schemes are analyzed.
status_evidence.claim: Synchro-betatron resonances induced by crab cavities have been characterized in part.

status_evidence.title: Impact of beam coupling impedance on crab cavity noise induced emittance growth
status_evidence.snippet: Couples impedance effects with crab-cavity noise.
status_evidence.claim: Additional beam-dynamics mechanisms continue to be uncovered, supporting partially_solved status.

status_evidence.title: Luminosity reduction caused by phase modulations at the HL-LHC crab cavities
status_evidence.snippet: Phase-modulation effects on HL-LHC luminosity quantified.
status_evidence.claim: Tolerances on phase modulation have been studied for HL-LHC.
